transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Maya Brooks (Redwood CSM); Michael Tan (Aurora Head of Platform), Sarah Lee (CTO), Raj Kapoor (ML Engineer), Elena Ortiz (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated for latency/cost and needs SOC2 + KMS for procurement.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll give a 30 minute walkthrough of the console and then leave time for Q&A. hi Michael, Sarah, Raj, Elena. can you hear us ok?
[00:06] Michael Tan: Yep, loud and clear. thanks Ethan.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Cool, quick agenda — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, and then routing/fallbacks and security.
[00:20] Sarah Lee: Sounds good. high level, our goals: reduce per-token spend, keep p99 latency under 250ms for chat flows, and ensure data doesn't leave our VPC.
[00:33] Ethan Morales: Perfect. we'll point out where those levers live in the console. ok Priya, take it away.
[00:38] Priya Shah: Sure. starting with the usage analytics page — this is the main cost and latency overview. you can break down by model, route, or api key. here's an example for last 30 days. you'll see token counts, token cost, and a token-level latency distribution. we also surface tail latency and broken-down compute vs storage costs. note: the transcript may show "tail latancy" in places, apologies for that.
[01:12] Raj Kapoor: when you say route, is that per endpoint path or per user route? how do you define it?
[01:20] Priya Shah: good question — route maps to the API route / named route you create in the Console routing rules. most teams create routes per feature, e.g., chat-reply, summarization-review. it can also be tied to API keys or customer ids.
[01:34] Daniel Park: and you can tag requests — so the dashboard can group by tag or route. that helps measure cost per product feature not just per model.
[01:43] Michael Tan: nice. can we see a cost explosion by route? like which feature is burning tokens?
[01:49] Priya Shah: yes, the per-route breakdown shows tokens, prompt vs completion split, and an estimated cost column using your pricing or our hosted rates. i'll open the per-route dashboard now.
[02:04] [screen share noises, links dropped - "console.redwood.ai/reports/route-costs" mentioned]
[02:12] Priya Shah: here you can see chat-reply is ~62% of token spend, vector-embed is 18%, and summarizer is 10%. we also show cost per unique user and cost per request.
[02:27] Sarah Lee: what's included in that cost calc? does it include batching and KV cache savings?
[02:33] Priya Shah: by default the dashboard uses nominal per-token rates. but there's a toggle to apply caching and batching adjustments — we simulate KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency so you can see best-case/worst-case cost.
[02:48] Raj Kapoor: how accurate is the KV cache sim? our prompt patterns are very prefix-heavy, hoping cache helps a lot.
[02:55] Priya Shah: we sample your traffic and estimate prefix reuse. it's an estimate, yes, not exact. for higher fidelity we recommend running a short pilot to measure actual cache hit rates.
[03:08] Michael Tan: that pilot — do you run it in our VPC or in Redwood hosted env? security team asks.
[03:15] Ethan Morales: two options — Hosted pilot (quick) or Dedicated VPC pilot (more effort but data never leaves your VPC). given your compliance needs we can propose a Dedicated pilot.
[03:26] Elena Ortiz: Procurement question — do you require an MSA before we run a pilot?
[03:31] Ethan Morales: usually we start pilots under an NDA + pilot agreement. procurement will see full contract language later.
[03:37] [05 sec pause]
[03:42] Daniel Park: back to the console, here's the per-route time series. you can set rolling windows, compare two routes, and break out by model variant — so if you have rwd-7b-quant vs rwd-13b it shows both.
[03:55] Raj Kapoor: what about quantized variants — do we lose quality? sometimes 4-bit causes hallucinations on our summarization tasks.
[04:03] Priya Shah: totally — we have a quality-monitoring feature in Optimize that ties a prompt set to a route and monitors metric regressions. you can set alerts if Rouge/BLEU/whatever drops. that helps you balance cost vs quality.
[04:20] Michael Tan: do you have an example of how a customer reduced costs with batching/caching?
[04:26] Priya Shah: yeah, we have a case — retail customer reduced per-token compute costs by ~35% by enabling prefix caching for session-history heavy chat flows and increasing batch windows for non-interactive endpoints.
[04:40] Sarah Lee: ok how does this translate to p99 latency? if we batch more we risk higher tail latency for chat.
[04:48] Daniel Park: right — there's a latency vs cost slider in the routing config. you can prefer low-latency nodes for chat-reply route while sending async summarization to cheaper pools. the console shows estimated p50/p95/p99 for each config.
[05:02] [06 sec cough]
[05:09] Priya Shah: now cost breakdown detail — token-level cost, compute vs memory (for private on-prem), and a chargeback view per team. you can export CSVs and connect to BI.
[05:22] Raj Kapoor: can we attribute costs to customer accounts inside Aurora? we need per-tenant billing for internal chargeback.
[05:29] Priya Shah: yes, the cost attribution supports tagging by tenant ids and can produce monthly reports.
[05:36] Michael Tan: security — KMS integration and audit logs, can you show relevant console pages?
[05:42] Priya Shah: sure switching to security tab. we support customer KMS, HSM integrations and provide a full audit log accessible in Console or via S3 export. note we also have redwood-private for VPC/on-prem where control plane sits in your network.
[05:59] Sarah Lee: SOC2 is a must for us. do you have recent attestation?
[06:05] Ethan Morales: yes, we are SOC 2 Type II. i'll share the report and the summary of controls after the call.
[06:12] Elena Ortiz: procurement needs a list of sub processors and data residency info.
[06:17] Ethan Morales: will include that in the doc pack.
[06:21] [short pause]
[06:25] Priya Shah: back to dashboards — here's a per-route cost drilldown: you can click any route and see the top contributing prompts, longest tokens, and outlier requests. we also highlight routes with rising error rates and token inflation.
[06:43] Raj Kapoor: "token inflation" — is that when you have prompt engineering regressions?
[06:46] Priya Shah: exactly — if a prompt change leads to longer completions or heavier system prompts, the analytics flags it. you can then roll back via rollout features.
[06:55] Michael Tan: rollouts — can we do canary on Dedicated? we want to validate model changes on a small percentage of users.
[07:01] Daniel Park: yes canary and A/B are supported, you can route a % of traffic to a variant and automatically rollback on error or quality regression.
[07:10] Sarah Lee: are metrics tied to our own evals? we have internal prompt tests.
[07:15] Priya Shah: you can upload an eval set and bind it to a route; Optimize will run periodic checks and alert on regressions.
[07:23] [screen flicker, a small laugh]
[07:28] Raj Kapoor: curious about pricing — how do you show cost per route? and what assumptions?
[07:33] Ethan Morales: the console uses your org pricing if you're on Dedicated; for Hosted we show default Redwood rates but you can upload negotiated rates. the per-route cost pulls token usage * per-token price + model-specific compute multipliers. we also model batching savings and cache hit assumptions if you enable those toggles.
[07:54] Michael Tan: can you export the assumptions? our finance team will want the calc.
[07:58] Priya Shah: yes exports include the calculation sheet. we'll share the workbook we used for these examples.
[08:05] Elena Ortiz: procurement again — if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum term?
[08:10] Ethan Morales: typically 12 month committed capacity but we can discuss flexible burst options. we'll include those SKUs in the pricing.
[08:19] [pause]
[08:25] Priya Shah: demoing alerts now — you can set quality thresholds and cost thresholds at route level. e.g., email Slack when summarizer cost per 1k reqs hits $x or when rouge score drops 5 points.
[08:42] Raj Kapoor: nice, we need the Slack integration.
[08:45] Daniel Park: Slack and PagerDuty integrations exist, plus webhook.
[08:50] Sarah Lee: question about fallback — if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can you fall back to hosted? we want resiliency.
[08:59] Priya Shah: yes, smart routing can failover to a compatible hosted variant. you define policies by latency/cost/region and specify fallback model variants.
[09:10] Michael Tan: in that case, how do you show blended cost in reports?
[09:15] Priya Shah: blended cost includes the fallback usage; the route report shows primary vs fallback split and cost per split.
[09:23] [timestamp jump — mid demo to cost spreadsheet]
[09:30] Priya Shah: switching to the cost spreadsheet — here we model three scenarios: hosted only, dedicated baseline, and dedicated + burst. for Aurora's traffic shape we estimate 22-28% cost reduction on dedicated baseline after factoring in caching and quantized models.
[09:49] Raj Kapoor: are those numbers assuming quantization to 4-bit? we are cautious about quality drop.
[09:54] Priya Shah: it's a mix — for non-chat summarization endpoints we use 4-bit quant, for chat we suggested 8-bit or carefully validated 4-bit. Optimize recommends quantization profiles per route.
[10:07] Sarah Lee: what's the uplift in engineering effort to run Private vs Dedicated?
[10:12] Ethan Morales: Dedicated is managed by Redwood but isolated capacity; Private (VPC/on-prem) requires more setup and network ops. We'll include a matrix in the doc pack.
[10:23] [11 sec pause]
[10:35] Michael Tan: customers have raised concerns about token visibility — can we mask user content in logs?
[10:41] Daniel Park: yes you can enable redaction for logs; we also support PII scrubbing and only logging metadata for some routes.
[10:49] Priya Shah: also note you can configure retention windows for usage analytics and export raw telemetry if you want to keep it in your S3.
[10:58] Raj Kapoor: ok pilot design — we want to test chat-reply and summarizer for 2 weeks, measure latency and cache hit. who will own the test?
[11:06] Sarah Lee: Raj will lead from Aurora.
[11:09] Raj Kapoor: ok i'll partner with Priya.
[11:12] Priya Shah: great, we'll draft a test plan and shared folder.
[11:17] Michael Tan: ROI question — finance will want upfront numbers for 6 and 12 months.
[11:22] Ethan Morales: we'll run sensitivity table in the pricing doc.
[11:26] Elena Ortiz: on procurement side we need vendor security packet and typical SLA.
[11:31] Ethan Morales: will include SLA terms and security packet.
[11:35] [short background noise]
[11:40] Daniel Park: quick note on monitoring — traces are integrated so you can see token-level timing, which kernel used for inference, and when fallback happened. some of the kernel names may translate oddly in the transcript as "kernel switcher".
[11:59] Raj Kapoor: can we do per-route retention — e.g., keep chat logs 30 days but summarizer logs 12 months?
[12:05] Priya Shah: yep retention policies are route configurable.
[12:10] Michael Tan: anything else on the console that helps reduce surprise bills?
[12:14] Priya Shah: budget alerts, spend ceilings, and simulated runbooks — you can set autoscaling thresholds to cap cost and route to cheaper pools automatically.
[12:27] Sarah Lee: final compliance push — can you confirm backup encryption and data residency controls?
[12:32] Ethan Morales: backups encrypted with customer KMS when requested; residency controls available per region.
[12:38] [pause]
[12:42] Priya Shah: almost done, last thing — Optimize suggestions: it surfaces batching windows, cache TTL suggestions, and recommended quant profiles by route with estimated delta in cost and expected quality impact.
[12:58] Raj Kapoor: useful. will the suggestions auto-apply?
[13:02] Priya Shah: they're recommendations; some can be auto-applied under a policy, most customers choose to review before applying.
[13:10] Michael Tan: ok let's summarize next steps.
[13:14] Ethan Morales: recap — Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated SKUs, SOC2 + security packet, per-route dashboard exports and a video walkthrough. Priya and Raj to scope pilot and define test prompts. Maya will follow up with notes and links.
[13:28] Elena Ortiz: procurement timeline — we aim to review doc pack by 3/16 and decide on pilot contracting shortly after.
[13:35] Ethan Morales: excellent. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the materials today.
[13:40] Sarah Lee: thanks all.
[13:43] [call ends]
